column1: # metrics group, build A (note 0009 D7.1, B07). Builder A, 2026-11-20.
# Sources: EasyMesh through the usp-spec MCP server (doc easymesh): §3.1.2 Conventions (bit/byte order per [2] = IEEE
#   1905.1, multi-octet integers big-endian; reserved objects set to zero by the sender, ignored by the recipient),
#   §17.2.62 Table 84, §17.2.73 Table 95. TLV codes from the tables match em-types codes.rs:280-287 (0x93-0x9a),
#   Upstream (pinned ba4180b, read from an extracted copy): em_metrics.cpp:1722-1904 (0x99 sender: one AP Channel Report
#   {len 2, op class, channel} at :1867-1882 unless caller reports with channel 255 at :1848-1865; Num_Ids + Element_List only when
#   req_params, Reporting Detail 1 and elements > 0 at :1885-1892; channel 0 falls back to 255 at :1816), :1907-1930
#   (0x9a), :1933-1990 (0x94: 0 octets when the BSS radio was not requested; committed at :1521), :1993-2032 (0xc7:
#   30 octets always; the buffer is zeroed by em_msg.cpp:605-609, so a BSS on an unrequested radio gives 30 zero
#   sizeof(em_assoc_wifi6_sta_sts_t) = 9, em_base.h:1355-1360; caller :1546-1549), em.cpp:1879-1902 (0xc5: memcpy of
#   a host u32, little-endian on x86_64; 0 octets when radio_cap is NULL; callers em_capability.cpp:231, :427).
#   201-203 (0xc8), 224-225 (0xb0). Every port_rule is SPEC or "-" except line 195 (0xc5): UPSTREAM, Collection
#   Interval little-endian (0008 D6). Line 200 is UNSURE (which BSSs are sent: consumer; D3). Note 0009 D2 (raw
#   reserved values, zero counts), D4 (0x99 lenient row), D5 (IEEE 802.11 content as raw octets), D8.
#   No table in this group says "one or more"; Tables 46, 48 and 84 say "if Num_... = 0, these fields are omitted".
#   Every zero count here is a spec case.
# Wire layouts (hex = tlvValue only; multi-octet integers big-endian per §3.1.2 except 0xc5):
#   0x94: AP_MAC(6), Utilization(1), Num_STA(2), octet {IncludeBE b7, IncludeBK b6, IncludeVO b5, IncludeVI b4,
#         Reserved b3-0}, EstServiceParametersBE(3, always), then BK(3) if IncludeBK, VO(3) if IncludeVO, VI(3) if
#         IncludeVI, in that order (BK, VO, VI; not bit order). The 3-octet ESP fields are raw octets (D5).
#   0x96: STA_MAC(6), Num_BSSID(1), Num_BSSID x { AP_MAC(6), time_delta(4), MAC_rate_down(4), MAC_rate_up(4), RCPI(1;
#   0x97: OpClass(1), Num_Chan(1), Num_Chan x { Channel_Number(1), Num_STA(1), Num_STA x STA_MAC(6) }. One OpClass per
#         TLV (audit 97): octets after the last channel are TrailingBytes.
#   0x98: OpClass(1), Num_STA(1), Num_STA x { STA_MAC(6), Channel(1), Time_Delta(4), RCPI(1; 221-255 raw) }.
#   0x99: STA_MAC(6), Operating Class(1), Channel Number(1), BSSID(6), Reporting Detail(1; raw), SSID Length(1),
#         SSID(SSID Length), Num_Report(1), Num_Report x { Report Length(1), OpClass(1), Channel List(Report Length - 1)
#         }, Num_Ids(1, always present), Element_List(Num_Ids). Report Length 0 cannot describe the bytes:
#         InvalidLength. Report Length 1 = empty Channel List.
#   0x9a: STA_MAC(6), Reserved(1), Num_Report(1), Num_Report x Measurement Report element { Element ID(1), Length(1),
#         Length octets }. The element is carried raw (D5); its ID is not checked.
#   0xa2: STA_MAC(6), BytesSent, BytesReceived, PacketsSent, PacketsReceived, TxPacketsErrors, RxPacketsErrors,
#   0xc5: Collection Interval(4, LITTLE-endian, audit 195 UPSTREAM). Exactly 4.
#   0xc6: RUID(6), Noise(1), Transmit(1), ReceiveSelf(1), ReceiveOther(1). Exactly 10.
#   0xc8: MAC Address(6), Num_BSSID(1), Num_BSSID x { BSSID(6), LastDataDownlinkRate(4), LastDataUplinkRate(4),
#   0xb0: MAC Address(6), Num_TID(1), Num_TID x { TID(1), Queue Size(1) } (both raw).
#   (1) Items are written in the listed order. Items named mac, bssid, ruid, sta_mac or ending in _mac are 6-octet MACs
#       (12 hex digits). num_sta (0x94): 2 octets BE. 4 octets BE: 0x96 bK_delta, bK_down, bK_up; 0x98 sK_delta; 0xa2
#       bytes_sent, bytes_recv, pkts_sent, pkts_recv, tx_errors, rx_errors, retrans; 0xc7 uni_sent, uni_recv,
#       multi_sent, multi_recv, bcast_sent, bcast_recv; 0xc8 bK_dl, bK_ul, bK_util_rx, bK_util_tx. 4 octets
#       LITTLE-endian: 0xc5 interval. Every other integer item is 1 octet. Values are decimal or 0x-hex.
#   (2) Byte-string items (esp_be, esp_bk, esp_vo, esp_vi, ssid, rK_chans, ids, rK_body) are hex: raw octets written
#       exactly as given, with NO length octet in front (lengths are the separate ssid_len, rK_len, num_ids items).
#   (3) Count and length items (bssids, chans, cK_stas, stas, reports, rK_len, num_ids, tids, ssid_len) are written as
#       given; only the entries listed follow (a count or length above the listed data = overstated). Entry names:
#       0x93/0x96/0xc8 bK_*; 0x97 cK_ch, cK_stas, cK_sJ_mac; 0x98 sK_*; 0x99 rK_len, rK_class, rK_chans; 0x9a rK_id,
#   (4) 0x94 bit-field octet: {inc_be b7, inc_bk b6, inc_vo b5, inc_vi b4, flags_reserved b3-0} is ONE octet, written at
#       the position of the group's first listed item; values unshifted (0/1); flags_reserved is a mask in octet
#       position, ORed in (absent = 0). 0x9a reserved is a whole octet item at its own position (0 = zero octet).
#       A case that sets reserved bits/octet: the decoder ignores them; the encoder writes zero (canonical bytes =
#   (5) An item given as hex: where it normally takes a MAC or integer is a cut field: exactly those raw octets are
#       written. An item not listed is absent from the bytes.
#   (6) trailing=hex: raw octets appended after the listed fields.
#   (7) kind=lenient;decoded=num-ids-zero (0x99 only): the bytes end after the AP Channel Report group with no Num_Ids
#       octet (the form em_metrics.cpp:1885-1892 writes). decode_value_lenient returns Ok(Some(body)) equal to the
#       strict decode of the sibling row named <case>-spec (same fields plus num_ids=0;ids=hex:), so re-encoding
#       gives that sibling's bytes. The strict decoder rejects every kind=lenient row with Truncated.
# Choices (for the coordinator): (a) every cut field, partial entry or overstated count/length is error=Truncated (as
#   B01-B06); extra octets after a complete layout are TrailingBytes; 0x99 Report Length 0 is InvalidLength (D2: a
#   length that cannot describe the bytes; precedent D3 line 222). (b) 0x94 IncludeBE=0 (bk-alone, vo-alone,
#   vi-alone, include-be-clear, reserved-bits-set-zero-flags) is kind=spec: "shall be set to one", but the BE field is
#   always 3 octets, so the flag sizes nothing (D2, value rule for the consumer). Conflicting precedent: channel group
#   choice (b), 0xa6 Fresh=0 with op classes = ValueOutOfRange. (c) 0x99 Num_Report > 0 with Channel Number != 255
#   (upstream-default-spec, upstream-detail-1-no-elements-spec) and Num_Ids > 0 with Reporting Detail != 1
#   (ids-with-detail-0) are kind=spec: well-formed bytes, value rules for the consumer (as cac choice (c)). If the
#   coordinator rejects them, upstream's default query form also needs the lenient path for Num_Report. (d) 0x99
#   Reporting Detail 3 and 0xff are carried raw (802.11 defines 0-2). A Channel List entry 255 (upstream's fallback,
#   audit 103) is a raw channel value. (e) 0x9a: Measurement Report elements are raw; an element ID other than 39
#   (other-element-id) and a 0-length element are kind=spec; an element Length above the remaining octets is
#   Truncated. (f) 0xb0 TID values above 7/15 are raw (kind=spec). (g) 0xb0 upstream-nine-zero-octets (the bytes
#   em_metrics.cpp:2299-2306 sends) is strict TrailingBytes; it is a lenient candidate for the user, not a lenient row.
#   (h) 0xc7 upstream-all-zero (30 zero octets, the unrequested-radio form) is kind=spec. (i) 0x94 upstream-be-zero is
#   upstream's normal agent form (BE flag 1, 3 zero octets).
